pageCache.text:
GLF Schools
Find out more about GLF Schools below.
Subjects
Music
We want our children to be engaged and inspired by music, in order to develop both musical talent and a lifelong love of the subject. As they learn to express themselves through singing, playing, improvising, and composing, children will develop the self-confidence to share their skills, understanding, and creativity.
Our music offer provides various opportunities to learn about new instruments and musical elements, both as a class and individually.
We develop oracy skills as children are exposed to appropriate musical terms and are encouraged to use these when discussing musical pieces.
We celebrate music and singing through performance and give our children opportunities to share their skills with different audiences such as in class assemblies.
Progression Document for Music is available via the link here.

pageCache.pageTitle: Art and Design - Art and Design - Subjects - Greenway Junior School
pageCache.text:
GLF Schools
Find out more about GLF Schools below.
Subjects
Art and Design
Art and Design give all children the opportunity to explore, develop and master new techniques in order to enhance their skills and knowledge. Our curriculum enables pupils to design, make and evaluate projects whilst learning and using technical vocabulary to describe processes. Children’s knowledge and understanding are deepened as the children study famous artists and designers.
We believe that Art and Design Technology gives children the skills, confidence and imagination that transfers into all subjects across the curriculum as well as in their wider lives.
Inspiring and nurturing their curiosity, interest, skills, and knowledge enables them to achieve in the subject. Through providing opportunities for the children to reflect on, and evaluate their work - both independently and collaboratively, they can take pride in their work and know how to develop it further.
The Progression Document for Art can be accessed via the link here.
Design Technology
We aim for Design and Technology to bring learning to life for the children. Skills such as designing, making, evaluating, and understanding technical knowledge in different circumstances and with different materials are engaging and rewarding for the children to participate in. Design and Technology provide a clear context for applying skills and knowledge from other areas of the curriculum including English, art, and maths. We want children to be given the opportunity to learn a wide range of new skills and build on those learned in previous years.
Through our design and technology curriculum, all children are encouraged to deepen their understanding of processes and the ability to problem solve.
The Progression Document for Design Technology can be accessed via the link here.

pageCache.pageTitle: Modern Foreign Languages - Modern Foreign Languages - Subjects - Greenway Junior School
pageCache.text:
GLF Schools
Find out more about GLF Schools below.
Subjects
Modern Foreign Languages
We aim to encourage all pupils to have an appreciation of other languages and cultures and, as such, consider the knowledge of modern foreign languages (MFL) to be essential to our children’s education.
We provide French lessons in each year group based on a progressive MFL scheme designed to ensure that new learning is introduced incrementally, applied, mastered, and then developed further.
In order to develop our children’s love of French, we include aspects of French culture and geography through our teaching in order to ensure that they have a context for their learning. By the end of Year 6, we aim for children to be able to speak, write, listen to and read a sentence in French independently, with knowledge of how the verb tense is formed.
The Progression Document for French can be accessed via the link here.

pageCache.pageTitle: History - History - Subjects - Greenway Junior School
pageCache.text:
GLF Schools
Find out more about GLF Schools below.
Subjects
History
At Greenway, we see the teaching of history as an opportunity for the children to develop their understanding of the development of the world around them, through a rich and varied curriculum.
Our history curriculum explores different time periods in specific year groups to provide learning opportunities that are exciting and engaging and develop children’s curiosity.
Our aim is to provide children with essential and transferable skills that will enhance their knowledge. Providing opportunities for children to think about, discuss and evaluate aspects from the past will expand their understanding and encourage their own lines of questions.
Our teaching of history aims to incorporate mastery skills and develop oracy through learning and applying key vocabulary, verbalising explanations, and sharing ideas with peers.
By the time the children finish Year 6, we want our children to have a sound understanding of chronology and the ability to apply this to a range of historical events, the skill to interpret and investigate a range of historical evidence, and be able to ask and interpret questions.
History Progression Document can be accessed via the link here.

pageCache.pageTitle: Maths - Maths - Subjects - Greenway Junior School
pageCache.text:
GLF Schools
Find out more about GLF Schools below.
Subjects
Maths
Our children learn through the White Rose Maths scheme, which believes in creating; 'a culture that produces strong, secure learning and real progress.' This scheme is aimed at providing children of all ability levels challenges through developing mastery skills across all areas of the maths curriculum.
Through having clear learning objectives, teaching and the use of resources are targeted at ensuring effective learning for all. Concepts are broken down into smaller steps for the children in order to ensure they are well-understood before progressing.
All children will be expected to understand and use accurate mathematical vocabulary when explaining their mathematical thinking, supported by clearly displayed maths vocabulary and working walls where relevant.
Number bonds and number facts are important for children to be able to quickly recall and as such we aim to teach, practise and reinforce these so that they can be applied by all children in their learning.
Progression Document for Maths is accessible via the link here.

PE
Our Physical Education curriculum encourages all children to understand how to look after their bodies. Our children engage in high-quality, active PE sessions which encourage the progression of their skills and abilities.
We want all children to develop a lifelong love for health and well-being, physical activity, and exercise.
Our PE curriculum nurtures and develops skills that all children can apply in other lessons and areas of their lives. Despite potential barriers to participation, all of our children are offered a broad range of extra-curricular and enrichment opportunities, which allows them to experience activities in different contexts and promote life-long habits.
Throughout their time at Greenway, the children's skills and knowledge will be supported and developed in order to ensure they achieve.

pageCache.pageTitle: English - English - Subjects - Greenway Junior School
pageCache.text:
GLF Schools
Find out more about GLF Schools below.
Subjects
English
At Greenway Junior School, we want all children to master the different aspects of English: reading, writing, listening, and speaking.
Reading
Equipping children with the knowledge and skills to decode, read and reflect on books will develop a love of reading that they will carry with them forever. Our library is supported by a variety of books in classes that will surround children and encourage their reading interest and development. We encourage parents and carers to share their child’s development in reading through the exploration of books, listening to their child read, and using differing question types to improve understanding.
Children develop their love of reading when there is partnership between home and school.
Writing
Opportunities to focus on the skills of writing provide the children with background knowledge that they will be able to apply in their writing to make it more interesting and creative.
Practising handwriting through our developmentally progressive handwriting scheme enables children to develop their skills in forming, joining and presenting their writing in ways that they can then apply directly into their work across the curriculum. Developing fluency and legibility in handwriting enables the children to directly see their skills when writing.
Oracy
Developing oracy skills through explicitly teaching and rehearsing key vocabulary and sentences, develops the children’s vocabulary and understanding of grammar. Mastering oracy is of the greatest importance to all areas of children’s learning, and providing structured opportunities throughout the curriculum provides the means to help achieve this for all children.
By the end of year 6, pupils’ reading and writing should be sufficiently fluent and effortless for them to manage the general demands of the curriculum in year 7, across all subjects. They should be able to reflect their understanding of the audience and purpose of their writing by selecting appropriate vocabulary and grammar.
The Progression Document for Reading can be accessed via the link here.

Find out more about GLF Schools below.
Subjects
Phonics
Phonics at Greenway Junior School is taught using the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised Scheme which has a clear rapid catch-up program suitable for meeting the needs of junior-age children.
The scheme follows a clear progression route for learning and applying phonic knowledge. All the graphemes taught are practised in words, sentences, and later on, in fully decodable books. Children who are not yet secure in their phonic knowledge review and revise it daily in order to move this knowledge successfully into their long-term memory.
The Progression Document for Phonics is available via the link here.

pageCache.pageTitle: RE - RE - Subjects - Greenway Junior School
pageCache.text:
GLF Schools
Find out more about GLF Schools below.
Subjects
RE
At Greenway Junior School, Religious Education is a meaningful and engaging part of the broad curriculum, which aims to help the children with their spiritual, moral, social, and cultural development in order to prepare them for the opportunities, responsibilities, and experiences of the present and the future.
We teach Religious Education through Discovery RE which is an enquiry-based scheme of work, covering the 6 principal world faiths.
Each enquiry lasts for half a term and begins with a “big” question such as “What is the best way for a Christian/Jew/Muslim etc. to show commitment to God?” The children then start discussing the theme of the enquiry (in this case, commitment) from their own experience. What have they shown commitment to? Brownies? Cubs? Their sporting team? Playing an instrument?
Only when the children fully understand the concept they are considering, do they move on to investigating what the people following the studied religion believe about it. The children will then apply their understanding through different activities that are often centred around a “big question”.
Our R.E. activities offer engaging and creative ways for children to explore and record their understanding - not just in writing.

Headteacher's Welcome
We are delighted to welcome you to Greenway Junior School.
We are proud to have joined GLF Schools on 1 September 2022, after a year of transition working with the multi-academy trust.
Greenway Junior School is a happy, safe and stimulating setting where children are motivated to learn.
Our broad and balanced curriculum is ambitious. It is taught with the consideration of the needs of all learners and is adapted to ensure that all children can achieve their full potential. Every child is recognised as a unique individual who is active in the learning process.
Please visit our learning pages to find out more.
Our core values of Integrity, Courage, Aspiration, Compassion and Respect ensure our pupils become active, positive and resilient young people.
We hope that our website provides a small insight into the vibrant school that we are, and the exciting journey that we are on. We would love to offer you an opportunity to come and view the school yourself. Please contact the office to arrange a visit.

GLF Spelling Bee
What an exciting day at the Spelling Bee! The children loved the warm-up word games before the competition began.
We competed in Heat 1 alongside 11 other schools and came 3rd, with two of our pupils making it to the final four contestants. By that stage, the spellings had reached secondary school level, exceptionally challenging!
Our team showed excellent teamwork, resilience and competitive spirit throughout.
Well done to all our participants, you've done Greenway Junior School proud!

pageCache.text:
GLF Schools

Horsham Children's Parade
The Children’s Parade on Sunday was a huge success, with children from across all year groups proudly taking part!
This year’s theme was Board Games, and Greenways fantastic creation of a Guess Who truly stood out, what a wonderful showcase of creativity, teamwork, and school spirit!
A big thank you to Mr Reed and Miss Wright and everyone who took part, helped prepare, and supported on the day. It was fantastic to see so many children and families come together for such a joyful community event!
